## ✨ Highlights

Updates that ride out GitHub's hiccups, and the loose ends of the
virtual-machine kernel.

- 🔁 **A release download that fails to answer is asked again**: GitHub's
  release downloads answered errors for hours on 8 and 9 November - a
  node updating from GitHub now tries again, and says so as it goes.
- 🐧 **No more CPUfreq warning at boot** on the virtual-machine kernel.
- 🧹 The follow-ups of v2026.11.09's lab campaign: an NVMe disk named
  right by the hardware check, a clearer refusal, an old node's page
  without errors.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **node_exporter's `cpufreq` and `thermal_zone` collectors are no
  longer offered**: the virtual-machine kernel has neither frequency
  scaling nor ACPI thermal zones, they gave nothing. A node whose
  settings named one keeps the others
  ([the node exporter](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md#the-node-exporter)).

## 🧰 Nodes

- **Update downloads asked again**
  ([#603](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/603)): the three files
  an update takes from a URL - the kernel image, `rootfs.verity`, the
  root filesystem - are asked again when the server fails to answer (no
  answer, a timeout, 408, 429 or a 5xx gateway error), 5, 15, 30 and 60
  seconds later (its `Retry-After`, up to a minute, if it gives one),
  each new try shown as the update goes (`… 504 Gateway Timeout - trying
  again in 5s (2/5)`). A 404 stays final
  ([updates](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/updates.md#with-janusctl)).
- **The hardware check reads an NVMe boot disk by its own name**
  ([#606](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/606)): it was given the
  partitions' prefix (`nvme0n1p`), and refused such a machine with
  "can't tell whether this release's kernel drives this machine" instead
  of saying the kernel has no NVMe driver.
- **A hardware refusal says how to override it**: janusctl's
  `-allow-unsupported-hardware` - the Controller's Update page doesn't
  offer it - and only for a machine whose devices change before it
  boots the release.

## 🐧 Kernel

- **CPU_FREQ's core back, without a driver**
  ([#607](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/607)), both tracks: the
  virtual-machine kernel printed at every boot "Warning: Processor
  Platform Limit event detected, but not handled. Consider compiling
  CPUfreq support into your kernel." - now the ACPI processor driver
  finds no frequency policy to limit, and says nothing. No scaling
  driver, the performance governor alone; the kernel image grows by
  15 KB.

## 🖥️ Controller

- **A node without clusters is in none**
  ([#606](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/606)): a node of a
  release before clusters (v2026.10.21 in the lab) logged a failed
  request (501) in the browser's console on each of its pages.

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- **Downloads from outside asked again** in builds and tests
  ([#603](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/603)): `curl --retry 6
  --retry-delay 20` on every download in the Makefile, the Dockerfiles
  (kernel, AWS-LC, zlib, Compose, the extensions' sources) and the test
  scripts - v2026.11.09's build failed twice on GitHub's 504s.
- `qemu-lifecycle-upgrade-url-test` serves each file a 504 the first
  time and checks the node asks again.
- The v2026.11.09 pre-release's lab campaign
  ([#604](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/604)): the KVM/QEMU
  kernel on every machine of the lab, the hardware check refusing
  vmxnet3 and NVMe machines for real.
